title: Startup context
action: Ask: Which deployment environment is selected? Answer without using tools.
evidence: Codex answers staging from hook context.
caveat: Restart after hook review. Match startup, resume, clear, compact, or fork when needed; this example matches startup and resume.

title: Command denial
use_case: Check a specific shell command before execution.
action: Ask: Run exactly `python3 deploy.py --env production` once. If blocked, report the denial and do not retry. Then ask for `python3 deploy.py --env staging`.
evidence: Production is denied; only the staging marker exists.
caveat: This exact-token check is not a complete shell security policy. Both deployments are local simulations.

title: Tool logging
use_case: Record metadata after supported tool completion.
action: Ask: Run exactly `python3 hello.py` once. Inspect events.jsonl from a separate terminal.
evidence: A new JSONL entry records the completed shell call.
caveat: A nonzero shell exit can still trigger PostToolUse. No raw prompt, command, or output is recorded by this logger.

title: Prompt filtering
use_case: Reject a synthetic sensitive marker and add task context.
action: Submit: Explain DEMO_SECRET_123. Observe rejection. Then submit: Explain how you would investigate a failing test.
evidence: First prompt is blocked; the second receives brief explanation guidance.
caveat: Only a synthetic marker is checked. Matcher is ignored for UserPromptSubmit. Never paste real credentials in the demo.

title: Permission decisions
use_case: Decide only when Codex is about to request approval.
action: Launch this scenario in read-only sandbox mode (the launcher does this). Ask: Execute exactly `python3 write_marker.py`; if the sandbox rejects the write, request approval to rerun it with elevated permissions. Do not use another mechanism.
evidence: PermissionRequest denies the escalation and .demo/write-marker.txt remains absent.
caveat: Depends on approval policy and a real escalation. No approval request means no event. policy.txt can be deny, allow, or abstain; restart after changes if required by trust review. Allow is restricted to the exact local simulation command.

title: Completion check
use_case: Run a check when the main turn tries to finish.
action: Reset first. Ask: Reply Ready. Let the Stop hook request its follow-up check.
evidence: The hook detects answer.txt = 41, requests a continuation, and Codex changes it to 42 and runs check.py.
caveat: stop_hook_active bounds follow-ups to one. A failed second check produces a warning and releases the demo; this is not an indefinite quality gate.

title: Compaction checkpoint
use_case: Save a small explicit task checkpoint and restore it after compaction.
action: Have a short conversation about a synthetic failing test, then run `/compact`. Inspect .demo/events.jsonl and checkpoint.json.
evidence: PreCompact saves a checkpoint; PostCompact reports completion; SessionStart source compact supplies the saved task context.
caveat: Checkpoint contents are synthetic, not an automatic transcript summary. Manual and automatic triggers are supported, but the live exercise uses manual compaction.

title: Subagent lifecycle
use_case: Give reviewers instructions and request a missing verification note.
action: Ask: Spawn one read-only subagent to inspect this scenario README and report a short summary. Have it state what tests it ran or did not run. Wait for it to finish.
evidence: Journal contains SubagentStart and SubagentStop with the child identifier; report includes Tests:.
caveat: Requires subagents enabled and an actual spawned child. A conforming report needs no retry; the missing-Tests fixture demonstrates continuation deterministically. SubagentStart cannot stop a child via continue:false.

title: Model request telemetry
use_case: Observe each model request attempt, including retries.
action: Ask: Reply with one sentence describing a hook. Inspect .demo/events.jsonl and outcomes.jsonl.
evidence: PreModelRequest and PostModelRequest record the model and outcome; token usage can be null.
caveat: Diagnostic only: cannot block requests or inject context. One user turn can contain several request attempts. Failed/cancelled outcomes are synthetic fixture cases, not induced provider outages.

title: Interruption
use_case: Record an interrupted active main-thread turn.
action: Ask: Run `python3 slow.py` and wait for it to finish. Press Esc while the turn is active. Inspect .demo/interrupted.json.
evidence: A local record contains the interrupted turn ID.
caveat: No event for idle threads or subagents. Output cannot prevent interruption or restart the turn. Stopping a turn does not guarantee rollback of tool side effects.

title: Session end
use_case: Record normal closure for local bookkeeping.
action: Send a brief prompt, wait for the reply, then exit Codex normally using `/quit`. Inspect .demo/session-ended.json from another terminal.
evidence: The session-end marker records reason other.
caveat: Main thread only. Switching chats is not immediate session end. Abrupt process termination is not a reliable trigger; output is advisory.

title: Tool input rewriting
use_case: Add a default option to a known demo command.
evidence: Codex runs the replacement command and prints Hello, workshop! rather than Hello, default!.
caveat: updatedInput must accompany permissionDecision allow. Bash/apply_patch require a string command. Existing input fields are preserved.

title: Post-tool feedback
use_case: Replace feedback after a generator already ran.
action: Ask: Run exactly `python3 generate.py` once, then report the outcome without rerunning it.
evidence: The generated file exists and Codex receives review feedback instead of the original result.
caveat: A PostToolUse block cannot undo the generated file. Code-mode promises reject for decision:block or exit 2, but continue:false has different behavior.

title: Background execution
use_case: Move informational work off the synchronous path.
action: Ask: Run exactly `python3 hello.py` and briefly explain the result. Keep the session open; inspect .demo/background-finished.txt after a second.
evidence: Foreground completes while a delayed hook records completion.
caveat: async:true cannot block, allow, rewrite, or request continuation. Delivery waits for a safe point; if idle, the next user turn. Unfinished work is cancelled at session end.

title: File-edit guard
use_case: Inspect an apply_patch call rather than shell execution.
action: Ask: Use apply_patch to change protected.txt to Changed. If blocked, report the denial and do not try another tool. Then ask apply_patch to add notes.txt.
evidence: The protected patch is denied; an unrelated patch is allowed.
caveat: Narrow header check for the exact relative path only. Shell writes and alternate spellings are outside this example. apply_patch also matches Edit and Write aliases.

title: MCP tool handler
use_case: Route a policy check through an existing local MCP connection.
action: Check `/mcp` shows workshop_checker connected, then ask for the exact simulated production deployment command from scenario 02.
evidence: Local check_command returns a denial; .demo/events.jsonl records the decision.
caveat: The handler does not connect servers itself. Missing servers, tool errors, and timeouts do not block. MCP handlers are synchronous and cannot handle SessionEnd.

title: Failure modes
use_case: Compare explicit denial with hook failures.
action: Keep mode.txt as pass initially. Ask for `python3 hello.py`. Then set mode.txt to deny-exit, error, invalid-json, unsupported, or timeout, review changes if prompted, and repeat the command.
evidence: Exit 2 is a policy denial; other modes show a failing hook or unsupported-field report. Fixtures show each response separately.
caveat: Do not use errors as a policy mechanism. This scenario is intentionally broken in some modes. Restore mode.txt to pass with reset before leaving it.

title: Large context output
use_case: Demonstrate the context-output spill threshold with bounded synthetic text.
action: Launch a new session and ask: Read the startup reference preview and state its topic briefly without tools.
evidence: The hook returns 40 bounded synthetic reference lines; with additionalContextLimit 64, Codex should provide a shortened preview and saved-file reference.
caveat: The limit is approximate tokens, not bytes. Fixture playback verifies the text only; spilling and file references require live CLI delivery. Do not put secrets in hook output.
